extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent attorneys/agents and applicants (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form paragraphs for handling Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs), related submissions/fees, examiner actions (including Quayle actions, appeals, suspensions), and claim/formal-matter issues in patent prosecution under MPEP §700.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995 that complies with 35 U.S.C. 371. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated throughout form paragraphs (e.g., 7.42.04–7.42.16, 7.42.11–7.42.14). Use these eligibility dates to determine whether to apply RCE procedures or to prepare a Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (PTO-2051) if RCE does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE fee requirement (37 CFR 1.17(e)) and timely payment
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination must include the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e); timely payment is required for the RCE to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee is missing (especially when filed after appeal/Board action), consequences vary: lack of fee may result in abandonment (if no allowed claims) or the submission not being entered (see ¶ 7.42.10–7.42.14). Insert in form paragraphs whether fee was timely paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required 'submission' content under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission under 37 CFR 1.114 may include an information disclosure statement (IDS), an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously filed arguments may be considered submissions if they are responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111. If the submission is absent or not entered, different form paragraphs apply (e.g., ¶¶ 7.42.10–7.42.14). Use bracketed items to identify date(s) and nature of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an RCE filed after allowance or Quayle action reopens prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE (with fee and submission) was filed after allowance or after an Office action under Ex parte Quayle, prosecution is reopened pursuant to 37 CFR 1.114 and the prior finality is withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.05 to acknowledge and insert the date(s) of receipt. Note that the submission may be prior amendments or accompanying amendment; follow MPEP and bracket instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after appeal but before Board decision withdraws appeal and reopens prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination filed after appeal to the PTAB but prior to a decision will withdraw the appeal if fee and submission are timely paid, and reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.06; note that an appeal brief need not have been filed. The submission may include arguments from appeal briefs or incorporation in the transmittal letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed after PTAB decision but before further appeal/civil action
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE is filed after a PTAB decision but before a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit or commencement of civil action, the appeal is withdrawn and prosecution is reopened (if fee and submission timely paid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.07. Note: a PTAB decision has res judicata/law-of-the-case effect; mere arguments without amendment or factual showing will not remove such rejection (see MPEP §§ 706.03(w), 1214.01). Be mindful of typical 63-day deadline to appeal to the Federal Circuit (MPEP §1216, 37 CFR 90.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission not fully responsive — shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE with fee and a submission is filed but the submission is not fully responsive to the prior Office action, applicant is given a shortened statutory period of TWO MONTHS from mailing to submit a complete reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.08; identify reasons why submission is not fully responsive in bracket 2. The shortened period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). This paragraph may be used regardless of whether the RCE was filed after final rejection, allowance, Quayle action, or appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination: special RCE responsiveness rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications granted special status under the accelerated examination program, if an RCE submission is not fully responsive, applicant is given a TWO (2) MONTH shortened period and must file replies electronically via EFS-Web to meet the 12-month objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.08.AE. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are possible but filing a petition for extension of time will remove the application from the accelerated program. Electronic filing is required to expedite processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: First action after RCE can be final — statutory reply periods
rubrics_metrics.description: A first Office action following filing of an RCE may be made final even though it is the first action after the RCE; a shortened statutory period for reply is set to expire THREE MONTHS from mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.09. If a first reply is filed within TWO MONTHS and the advisory action is mailed after the THREE-MONTH period, the shortened period will expire on the advisory action mailing date; in no event will the statutory period for reply expire later than SIX MONTHS from mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filed on appeal without required submission/fee — abandonment when no allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE filed after appeal lacks the fee required by 37 CFR 1.17(e) and/or the submission required by 37 CFR 1.114, and there are no allowed claims, the application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.10; this applies when RCE is filed after Notice of Appeal or appeal brief but before a decision. Insert dates in brackets and consider MPEP §1215.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE on appeal lacking submission but claims allowed — pass to issue on allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE filed after appeal includes the fee but lacks the required submission, and there are allowed claims, the appeal is withdrawn and the application will be passed to issue on the allowed claims; rejected claims are considered terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.11; cancel dependent/rejected claims as appropriate (insert canceled claim numbers). Use with Notice of Allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE on appeal lacking submission with formal matters outstanding — contingent pass to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If RCE includes fee but lacks submission and there are allowed claims with outstanding formal matters, the application will be passed to issue on allowed claims provided the formal matters are promptly corrected within a TWO-MONTH shortened period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.12; explain formal matters in bracket 3; extensions of time may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE on appeal lacking fee but includes submission — submission not entered; pass to issue on allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When an RCE filed after appeal includes a submission but lacks the fee required by 37 CFR 1.17(e), the submission is not entered and, if there are allowed claims, the application will be passed to issue on those allowed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.13; cite 37 CFR 1.116(c) and MPEP §1215.01; insert canceled claim numbers where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE on appeal lacking fee with formal matters outstanding — contingent pass to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If an RCE after appeal includes a submission but lacks the fee, and there are allowed claims with outstanding formal matters, the application will be passed to issue on allowed claims provided the formal matters are corrected within TWO MONTHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.14; explain the formal matters in bracket 3; extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA may be treated as RCE (design applications only for CPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a continued prosecution application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d) may only be filed in a design application; an improper CPA filed in a non-design application will be treated as an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.15 to advise applicant. Also use applicable RCE form paragraphs (7.42.04–7.42.07) to acknowledge entry of submission if fee timely paid. If fee/submission missing, follow 7.42.10–7.42.14 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE filed after Board decision without submission/fee — not tolled
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed after a PTAB decision but lacking the fee and/or submission is improper and any time period running was not tolled by filing the improper request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.16; when time for seeking court review has passed, use with Notice of Allowability or Notice of Abandonment as appropriate, or on PTOL-90 if time remains. Generally, do not enter submissions filed with improper RCE unless amendment obviously places application in condition for allowance (see MPEP §1214.07).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim objected as depending on rejected base claim but allowable if rewritten independently
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.43 to inform applicant that claim would be allowable if rewritten; include specific claim numbers in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable subject matter for claims rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (indefiniteness) — rewrite/amend to overcome rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A noted independent or dependent claim rejected solely on the basis of 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (pre-AIA second paragraph) would be allowable if rewritten or amended to overcome the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 7.43.01 and 7.43.02; used when rejection under 112(b) is sole basis and rewriting/amending would cure the rejection. For dependent claims, include limitations of base and intervening claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable subject matter with formal requirements outstanding — applicant must comply or traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: As allowable subject matter has been indicated, applicant's reply must either comply with all formal requirements or specifically traverse each requirement not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.43.03; appropriate when drawing corrections or specification corrections must be made prior to allowance. Cite 37 CFR 1.111(b) and MPEP §707.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner-suggested allowable claim(s) presented to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may draft suggested claim(s) considered to distinguish patentably over the art of record and present them to applicant for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.43.04; insert 'is' or 'are' and full text of suggested claim(s) in the bracketed items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification fails to provide proper antecedent basis — correction required
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification is objected to as failing to provide proper antecedent basis for the claimed subject matter; specific corrections are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.44; cite 37 CFR 1.75(d)(1) and MPEP §608.01(o); identify the corrections in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper multiple dependent claims — form objection under 37 CFR 1.75(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: A multiple dependent claim objected to under 37 CFR 1.75(c) as being in improper form because it should refer to other claims in the alternative only and/or cannot depend from another multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.45; indicate whether claim 'has' or 'have' not been further treated on the merits. Use this paragraph rather than 35 U.S.C. 112(e) or pre-AIA fifth paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment not entered if it unduly interferes with Office action preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment may not be entered if entry would unduly interfere with preparation of the Office action (37 CFR 1.115(b)(2)), e.g., examiner had completed significant work before receipt of the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.46; in brackets provide date of receipt, state of preparation, and explanation of additional time required (e.g., new prior art search or extensive revision). Advise applicant to resubmit amendment with responsive reply if not final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to present claims for interference may constitute disclaimer (AIA-specific caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to present claims and/or take necessary steps for interference after notification that interfering subject matter is claimed constitutes a disclaimer of the subject matter, amounting to a concession that the patentee is the first inventor (In re Oguie).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.48.aia only in applications examined under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 where there is an earlier effective filing date claim (or specific references) per bracketed conditions. Use only after applicant has been notified and has refused to copy claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse Board judgment and failure to appeal — final disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: An adverse judgment entered by the Board against claim(s) results in final disposition of those claims for failure to reply to or appeal within the time for appeal or civil action specified in 37 CFR 90.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.49; adverse judgment is a final action requiring no further Office action to dispose of the claim permanently (cite 37 CFR 41.127(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously allowed claims can be withdrawn in view of newly discovered art
rubrics_metrics.description: The indicated allowability of a claim may be withdrawn in view of newly discovered reference(s); rejection(s) based on newly cited references will follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.50; insert the newly discovered reference(s) and the statutory basis (e.g., 102(g) or 102(g)/103(a)). Actions including this paragraph require a Primary Examiner signature (MPEP §1004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quayle action: prosecution closed on merits; allowance contingent on formal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Ex parte Quayle practice, application may be in condition for allowance except for formal matters; prosecution on the merits is closed and a shortened statutory period for reply is set (typically TWO MONTHS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.51 (and 7.51.AE for accelerated). Explain formal matters to be corrected in bracket 1. For accelerated cases, the shortened period is TWO (2) MONTHS and filing for extensions may remove accelerated status. Cite Ex parte Quayle, 25 USPQ 74.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action awaiting new reference — limited duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte prosecution is SUSPENDED for a period of [1] months from mailing when a relevant reference may soon become available; maximum suspension period is six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.52; only the Technology Center (TC) Director can grant a second or subsequent suspension (MPEP §1003) and such approval must appear on the Office letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d), granted
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant's request for deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) may be approved, deferring examination for a specified number of months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.54.01; insert filing date of request and number of months for deferral in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of a suspension of action (applicant's request), granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's request for termination of a suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103 may be approved and the suspension terminated on the mailing date of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.54.02; note maximum suspension is six months, TC Director approval for subsequent suspensions, and that TC Director signature must appear on letters granting second/subsequent suspensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action due to possible interference — limited period
rubrics_metrics.description: When all claims are allowable but a potential interference exists, ex parte prosecution is suspended for a period of [1] months (maximum six months) pending interference determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.53; TC Director must approve second/subsequent suspensions (MPEP §1003) and their signature must appear on the letter.
